changelog: schema_version 3: follow-up cross-build static RE resolves the generic XDB ABI and corrects the earlier count interpretation. word0 is field_count and word1 is record_count; +0x18 is a packed 2-bit per-field type table; the row-major int16 descriptor matrix is selected by func_001AD180. For xdbboxr this means 121 fields x 37 records. SelectBoxer rating field IDs 0x10-0x18 are now mapped. Follow-up SelectBoxer tracing proves xdbboxr field 0x04 gates the 35-entry active stock roster.

header_word0_proof.claim: xdb header word0 is the field/column count, not the record count.
header_word0_proof.evidence: func_001ACCAC rejects field_id >= header.word0 and reads the corresponding 2-bit field type from payload+0x18+(field_id>>2). func_001AD268 independently loops exactly word0 times while classifying those same field types.
header_word0_proof.correction: The older 'per-entry count, possibly boxer rows' interpretation is superseded.

revised_header_model.claim: The generic XDB layout is field_count=word0, record_count=word1, packed two-bit field types at +0x18, followed (aligned) by a row-major signed-int16 descriptor matrix that ends at section_size_a.
revised_header_model.evidence: func_001AD180 bounds record_index against word1, computes matrix_start = section_size_a - align4(word0*word1*2), and selects row + record_index*(word0*2). func_001ACCAC bounds field_id against word0. func_001ACD40 maps type codes 0/1/2/3 to inline int16, string, int32, and float32 storage. The matrix-start formula lands immediately after the aligned type table in all 10 tracked XDB resources.

traced.proven_behavior: Masks its single argument to 8 bits ($a0 & 0xFF) -- this is a directly proven, concrete fact: the boxer index/ID parameter accepted by this accessor is 8 bits wide. It then calls the singleton accessor and walks a linked list starting from the returned singleton, dereferencing each visited node's +0x10 field up to 'index' times, stopping early if a node is null.
traced.unresolved_question: Whether each node visited by this walk is one boxer record, one loaded-table-instance registration, or some other chained object -- see static-resolution-matrix.json.

traced.proven_behavior: Calls the singleton accessor, then passes the result into a second shared generic function (func_001A0D78) not disassembled in this pass.

Calls the boxer-table singleton, constructs a record accessor via func_001ACFAC, then selects the requested record through func_00186284. Follow-up tracing reaches the generic field binder func_001ACD40 and the real SelectBoxer rating reader.

Constructs an object ($a0): initializes a sub-object at +0x18 (size 0x34, via shared function func_001A1638), stores a fixed vtable-like pointer (D_005817F4) at +0x14, initializes another sub-object at +0x50 (via the same generic initializer func_001A0AE4 used to construct the boxer singleton itself), calls the boxer singleton accessor, then calls func_001AD268(dest=+0x50 sub-object, singleton, stride=1). Stores a 16-bit result from a further call (func_0018654C) at +0x4C, then calls func_0018E60C before returning the constructed object.
traced.significance: The +0x14 vtable-like pointer and +0x18 sized sub-object strongly suggest this constructs a small, well-defined C++-style object type (not raw scratch memory), and its direct call into func_001AD268 with the boxer singleton is the clearest evidence found of code that specifically reads and reshapes boxer-table data for another consumer.
traced.unresolved: No caller of T_0018E4F4 was found anywhere in BOOT.BIN's 24,576 disassembled functions -- it may be reached only via a function pointer/vtable dispatch the static xref pass does not resolve, or from a different module/PRX not analyzed here.

traced.proven_behavior: Proven fight-session singleton constructor. It initializes internal XDB-derived sub-objects at +0x19F4 and +0x1A08, calls the boxer singleton accessor and func_001AD268 for each using caller-selected output strides 5 and 0x28, stores 16-bit follow-up results at +0x198C/+0x198E, and then initializes the remaining fight-session subsystems.
traced.significance: This embeds boxer/XDB-derived classification state directly in the fight-session object, alongside the now-mapped session mode, venue and per-corner boxer selection fields.
traced.unresolved: Exact semantic role of the two classification outputs at +0x198C/+0x198E and the remaining constructor substructure.

consumers.notes: These 6 functions (including the loader trampoline func_001863B4 itself) are exactly the complete set of direct callers of func_00186408 found by a whole-binary text search across all 24,576 disassembled functions in BOOT.BIN. All 6 have now been disassembled and interpreted in this pass (5 in the prior pass plus T_0018E4F4/func_001AF768 newly this pass -- 6 total across both passes, with func_00186464/func_001863E4/func_00185114 carried over from the earlier pass). No other function in BOOT.BIN references the boxer table singleton accessor by name; a caller could in principle still reach the singleton indirectly, or the singleton's raw address (0x80B4) could be hardcoded elsewhere without going through the accessor -- a direct-address search found zero such references, but that does not rule out access via a relocated pointer computed at runtime.

fixed_counts_and_limits.claim: Boxer index/ID parameter to func_00186464 is masked to 8 bits (0-255).
fixed_counts_and_limits.caveat: This proves the accessor's own parameter width, not the database's own record-count field.

fixed_counts_and_limits.claim: xdbboxr.adf has 121 fields and 37 records in the tracked retail resource.
fixed_counts_and_limits.evidence: word0=121 is bounded as field_count by func_001ACCAC; word1=37 is bounded as record_count by func_001AD180.
fixed_counts_and_limits.caveat: 37 is the current resource row count read dynamically from the header; this does not establish a separate hard maximum.

cross_resource_relationships.relationship: preload/tables.viv hairstyle files <-> preload/bootpreloads.viv HK_*.bh preload descriptors <-> repository-root hk_*.viv archives
cross_resource_relationships.evidence: This pass found and enumerated 36 repository-root hk_*.viv archives, confirming two distinct kinds by direct content inspection: (1) 28 generic hairstyle-template archives (hk_afro1.viv, hk_aight.viv, hk_braid.viv, ...) each containing a full morph-target set (cranium shape x8 directions, ears x4, forebrow x2, headgear compatibility, plus a mod_hair_<style>.o base model); (2) 8 named-legend-boxer archives (hk_ali.viv, hk_hatto.viv, hk_lazca.viv, hk_leona.viv, hk_moral.viv, hk_pacqu.viv, hk_punch.viv, hk_robin.viv) each containing exactly one bespoke mod_hair_<name>.o model. The 8 named archives' stems match exactly bootpreloads.viv's 8 HK_*.bh descriptors and 7 of tables.viv's boxer-surname .txt files (the 8th, 'punch'/'punchout.txt', now reads far more plausibly as a hairstyle-template alias rather than a placeholder, since it sits alongside 'aight' in a naming pattern of short colloquial style nicknames).
cross_resource_relationships.why_upgraded_from_candidate: The prior pass's finding rested on filename-stem matching alone across two archives. This pass independently verified the content of all 36 archives directly (not just their names), confirming the two-kind split (generic style vs. named-legend) is a real structural distinction proven by member enumeration, not an assumption from filenames.
cross_resource_relationships.why_not_confirmed: No executable code path connecting hk_*.viv, bootpreloads.viv's HK_*.bh descriptors, and tables.viv's boxer-surname .txt files was traced in this pass; the relationship is still established by content/name correspondence, not by a shared consumer function.

cross_resource_relationships.relationship: boxersh.viv / cboxshr.viv / boxmisc.viv / boxmisc2.viv <-> boxer appearance and damage systems
cross_resource_relationships.evidence: All 4 archives are listed together in the 9-entry resource registry table found in BOOT.BIN (see resource-loader-map.json), alongside boxerpre.viv, actors.viv, allhair.viv, and tables.viv. Content confirms strong topical relevance: boxersh.viv contains staged damage.msh/damage_0/1/2.msh models (direct evidence of a leveled damage-visualization system) plus glove models; cboxshr.viv contains numbered/patterned shorts models (direct match to tables.viv's shorts.csv target); boxmisc.viv contains face.off/face_cuts.off (direct medical/damage relevance) plus fringe/gravity_head/hilite/laces geometry; boxmisc2.viv contains headgear-compatibility hair morph targets keyed by the same short-codes as the root-level BL_<code>.viv per-boxer archives.
cross_resource_relationships.why_not_stronger: No executable code path from these 4 archives to any specific boxer record, Medical function, or equipment field was traced in this pass; the registry table proves they are all managed together as one resource family, not that any specific field of xdbboxr.adf selects among them.

cross_resource_relationships.evidence: Both archives contain the identical 167 member names in the identical order with identical per-member sizes. scripts.viv's members are RefPack-compressed; scrptpal.viv's are not. For the sampled member 'addanims.bin', decompress_refpack(scripts.viv member) and the raw scrptpal.viv member are the same length (248 bytes) and share the same 4-byte magic ('stp\x01') plus most byte positions, but differ at specific integer fields. This proves the two archives hold two distinct, same-shaped parameter sets for the same named script entries -- not that one is a decompressed duplicate of the other.
cross_resource_relationships.open_question: Deferred to program-05/06 static analysis (fight-engine scripts), out of Task 10/11 scope -- see static-resolution-matrix.json.

cross_resource_relationships.relationship: preload/boxerpre.viv and actors.viv/boxmisc.viv damage/morph geometry <-> program-10 (Medical)
cross_resource_relationships.evidence: boxerpre.viv's 8 mor_base_head_dam*.o members, actors.viv's face_hires.off/face.off/swelltool.off, and boxmisc.viv's face_cuts.off are all named for facial damage/swelling/cut visualization, structurally consistent with the Medical subsystem's stoppage/damage path. No executable code path was traced connecting any of these archives to a Medical-owning function in this pass.

12 base venue/location names exist under enviro/. The recovered XDB ABI proves xdbvenue.adf word1=12 is its record count (word0=9 fields). Independently, func_001B00A0 accepts venue IDs only while signed venue_id < 12. These three facts converge on a 12-record venue table.
cross_resource_relationships.why_not_stronger: The exact mapping of each of the 12 XDB venue records to the 12 asset-name stems has not yet been traced field-by-field.

stock_selectboxer_availability.conclusion: Field 0x04 is the stock SelectBoxer inclusion/availability gate. Rows 0-34 all carry 1; bonus rows 35-36 carry 0 and are outside this 35-slot initializer. A separate bonus unlock mechanism, if any, is not inferred from this path.
